subject: Life Skills
title: Hedonic Adaptation and Spending
description: A 60-second lesson on Hedonic Adaptation and Spending.

hook.text: He bought the car of his dreams. Joy lasted three weeks. By month two, it was just his car. He wanted the next one.

buildup.text: Hedonic adaptation means you return to a baseline happiness level after any purchase.

discovery.text: Research shows experiences resist adaptation better than objects. A great trip stays vivid.

twist.text: Upgrades become the new normal instantly. Once you fly business class, economy feels like punishment.

climax.text: Before a big purchase, ask: will I still feel this way in six months? If not, the joy is temporary and the cost is not.

punchline.text: The thrill fades. The bill stays. Choose wisely.

quiz.question: Why do experiences resist hedonic adaptation better than objects?
options: Memories stay vivid while objects become invisible background
People value experiences more because they cost less
